topic: External model evaluators and enterprise assurance
angle: What third-party evaluation inside AI labs should change for enterprise buyers
sourceTitle: AI Companies’ New Plan to Keep Themselves From Destroying Everything
linkedinPost:
“Independent oversight” of AI models sounds reassuring—until you read the fine print.

A piece in The Atlantic examines AI companies inviting third-party evaluators inside. The open question: how much access, and what influence, do they really have over models and deployment decisions?

From the enterprise seat, external audits only matter if they change buyer behavior. My take from FDE work: ask vendors for evidence you can operationalize—reproducible evals on your data, risk reports mapped to your use cases, and remediation SLAs tied to incidents.

I’ve watched too many pilots wave at generic benchmarks while production fails on edge cases no one measured. “We were evaluated” isn’t an assurance statement; a signed, scoped test plan with acceptance criteria is.

If third-party evaluators become a norm, buyers should align them to procurement gates: pre-award model fitness, pre-go-live controls, and post-incident reviews. Otherwise, audits drift into theater and your team carries the risk anyway.

Question to leaders: If a vendor claims independent oversight, what exact artifacts would let you approve go-live with confidence—and which would still be nice-to-have? #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
